name: Victor Hugo
role: French novelist, peer, republican deputy and senator (1802-1885)
summary: Hugo moved from royalism to a republicanism that joined universal suffrage and free press with lay free schooling, abolition of the death penalty, public relief and a federal United States of Europe. He opposed Louis Bonaparte's coup and lived in exile for nearly twenty years, defended property while wanting it spread to workers, and backed colonisation as a duty of tutelage for 'elder' peoples.

notes: Read from his own collected speeches and pamphlets (Actes et Paroles I-III, Napoleon the Little, History of a Crime). His early royalism and Catholicism (before about 1848) are not used: answers reflect the mature republican position held from the 1848 Assembly to his death; the later speeches of 1876-1885 and the 1879 banquet addresses were not read.
